fluff.overview: The Vandal is a 65-ton Inner Sphere OmniMech introduced in 3142 by the Capellan Confederation. Produced by StarCorps Industries at their St. Ives facility, the design was developed under tight security to fill a heavy cavalry role for the Confederation's expanding military ambitions. The Vandal combines respectable speed with substantial firepower and advanced electronics, making it an effective team player in combined-arms formations. Its combination of networking capability, electronic warfare systems, and raw speed has made the Vandal a mainstay of Capellan heavy formations, with production continuing at St. Ives to meet growing demand from both Confederation forces and allied states.
fluff.capabilities:
The Vandal is built on a StarCorp 120-Flex Endo Steel frame powered by a VOX 325 XL engine, giving the 65-ton design a respectable top speed of 86 kilometers per hour. A fixed Supercharger allows MechWarriors to push the engine to 108 kph in short bursts, granting the Vandal exceptional speed for a heavy OmniMech and enabling effective cavalry tactics. The chassis provides 26.5 tons of pod space, a generous capacity that allows each configuration to carry substantial weaponry and equipment. The design mounts 12.5 tons of ArcShield VII Mk.8 standard armor with CASE II protection in the right torso, providing solid battlefield survivability while protecting ammunition stores from catastrophic detonation.

A distinguishing feature of the Vandal is its Torso-Mounted Cockpit, which affords the pilot greater protection at the cost of more difficult emergency ejections. All three original configurations incorporate some form of C3 boosted networking capability, emphasizing the Confederation's doctrine of coordinated lance-level fire. The inclusion of Angel ECM Suites in multiple configurations further enhances the design's electronic warfare profile. While the lack of jump jets limits the Vandal's terrain flexibility, its raw speed and electronic warfare capabilities make it a formidable opponent in open engagements.
fluff.history:
The Vandal's origins trace to a cache of long-abandoned OmniMech schematics recovered by StarCorps Industries at their St. Ives facility. Working under strict Capellan Confederation security protocols, engineers adapted these designs into a modern combat platform, with development proceeding in such secrecy that no foreign intelligence service detected the project before the Vandal reached active service in 3142. The design was rushed into production to support the Confederation's ambitious military campaigns in the 3140s.

The Vandal first saw combat during the Capellan invasion of the Federated Suns, making its battlefield debut on Spica in late 3144. Several lances of Vandals championed the assault, with elements of multiple CCAF regiments storming the border world in a lightning offensive. The Vandals blazed past hastily assembled defensive positions and struck at rear echelon formations before Federated Suns defenders could establish a coherent defense. The C3 boosted networking proved devastatingly effective, allowing Vandal lances to coordinate fire with accuracy far exceeding what their numbers would suggest.

On Demeter, Warrior House Ijori employed Vandals during the storming of New Demeter City. Rather than bypassing the front lines, the fast Ijori elements used their Vandals' C3 networks to combine fire and savage AFFS defenders. When opposing forces deployed powerful ECM systems, the Vandals demonstrated their capability as individual combatants, executing precision tactics that overwhelmed the city's defenders even without network support. Demeter fell in mid-December.

The Vandal also proved effective in the hands of Capellan allies. During a joint Canopian-Andurien Cavalry raid on Glevakha in March 3145, raiding forces encountered the elite Fourth Rim Commonality Guards conducting arctic-alpine training in the Kyyivska Peaks. Despite the raid's original reconnaissance intent, the heavy-mineral terrain masked the Guards until the raiders swept nearby cities. The Guards launched a counterattack from the slopes, eventually forcing an assault on the raiders' DropShips. Vandals led the defensive effort, their combination of speed and firepower holding off the Guards long enough for the raiding force to withdraw.

Production has continued at St. Ives, with the Vandal seeing deployment not only with Confederation regular forces and Warrior Houses but also with allied states including the Magistracy of Canopus.
fluff.deployment: Alternate Configuration A serves as the command vehicle for a C3 boosted lance, mounting a C3 boosted master unit in place of the slave found in other configurations. Its primary weapon is a Heavy PPC enhanced by a PPC Capacitor in the left arm, capable of delivering devastating alpha strikes at range. A four-tube Short-Range Missile launcher with a single ton of ammunition provides close-range punch, while a Laser Anti-Missile System in the right arm offers defense against incoming missiles. Four jump jets give this configuration a mobility advantage over the other Vandal loadouts, allowing its commander to reposition quickly and maintain optimal firing positions for the entire lance. An additional double heat sink helps manage the considerable thermal output of the capacitor-enhanced PPC.
